# Class: Engine3D

Defined in: [src/Engine3D.ts:76](https://github.com/orillusion/orillusion/blob/main/src/Engine3D.ts#L76)

Orillusion 3D Engine.

Call `await Engine3D.init({ canvasConfig, setting })` to obtain an
engine instance. Each instance owns its canvas, input system, views,
render jobs, and configuration (`engine.setting`). Instances share a
single WebGPU device pool and a shared RAF render loop.

###### render.gpuCull?

`boolean`

GPU-driven culling — when true, frustum + (when paired with
 Hi-Z) occlusion tests run on the GPU per mesh instance and
 produce a `drawIndexedIndirect` arg buffer. The compute pass
 is fully implemented in `GPUCullPass` / `GPUFrustumCull_cs`;
 what's still skeleton is the `drawNodes` consumer
 (`_transparentDraw.ts`, driven by `ColorPass`) that actually
 issues the indirect call (the existing per-node iteration
 coexists). Flip this on AND open the integration in `drawNodes`
 to get the 5-20× perf win.

###### render.msaa?

`0` \| `2` \| `4` \| `8`

Per-instance MSAA sample count for the main color pass.
 0 disables MSAA (default). Valid non-zero values: 2 | 4 | 8
 depending on device support. Enabling MSAA unlocks
 alpha-to-coverage (set LitMaterial.alphaMode = 'MASK').

###### render.useOIT?

`boolean`

Opt-in order-independent transparency (Weighted Blended OIT).
 When true, materials with `oitMode === 'weighted'` are routed
 through the OIT accum/resolve features instead of the sorted
 transparent path. Default false — matches legacy behavior.

###### render.decals?

`boolean`

Opt-in projected decals. When true, ForwardRendererJob inserts
 `DecalShadowVolumePass` between the opaque/transmission half and
 the sorted transparent half — every active `DecalComponent`
 projects its texture onto the opaque scene via stencil shadow
 volumes. Default false.

###### render.useStencil?

`boolean`

Opt-in 8-bit stencil buffer on the main color pass.
 When true, `GBufferFrame` allocates its depth attachment as
 `depth24plus-stencil8` instead of the default `depth32float`,
 so material-level stencil state (`Material.stencilFront/Back/
 ReadMask/WriteMask/Ref`) is actually validated and bound at
 pipeline build time. Off by default — adding stencil makes the
 depth attachment incompatible with depth-only sampling paths
 (SSR/SSGI/Outline read `_MainDepthTexture` as `sampleType: depth`),
 so opt in only when the project actually needs stencil and the
 z-prepass is disabled (`zPrePass: false`) — the prepass path
 routes the color pass through a separate `depth32float`
 `zPreTexture` and the stencil attachment is silently dropped.

###### render.tonemap?

\{ `enable?`: `boolean`; `exposure?`: `number`; `mode?`: `"ACES"` \| `"None"`; \}

Final HDR→LDR tonemap. Runs after every other post (Bloom,
FXAA, GodRay, etc.) so the ACES curve sees the composited HDR
signal. Setting `enable=false` reverts to a passthrough pass —
lighting and bloom shaders no longer apply inline ACES, so the
frame will be raw HDR clamped at swapchain encode time.

###### render.tonemap.enable?

`boolean`

Master switch. When false, the post is still attached but
 acts as a straight passthrough — useful for A/B comparisons.

###### render.tonemap.exposure?

`number`

Linear scale multiplied onto the HDR color before the curve.
 1.0 is the neutral default (no exposure compensation).

###### render.tonemap.mode?

`"ACES"` \| `"None"`

Curve selector. 'ACES' applies the Filmic Narkowicz fit;
 'None' is straight passthrough (same effect as enable=false
 but keeps exposure scaling).

###### render.postProcessing.taa?

\{ `enable?`: `boolean`; `jitterSeedCount?`: `number`; `blendFactor?`: `number`; `temporalJitterScale?`: `number`; `sharpFactor?`: `number`; `sharpPreBlurFactor?`: `number`; `debug?`: `boolean`; \}

###### render.postProcessing.taa.enable?

`boolean`

###### render.postProcessing.taa.jitterSeedCount?

`number`

The number of random seed for dithering camera is 8 by default.
Reducing the number can solve some problems with noticeable jitter, but the jagginess will become more pronounced

###### render.postProcessing.taa.blendFactor?

`number`

Merge the coefficients of the historical frame and the current frame. The smaller the parameter, the smaller the proportion of the current frame

###### render.postProcessing.taa.temporalJitterScale?

`number`

The scaling coefficient of the random offset value of the jitter camera [0,1]: The smaller the coefficient, the weaker the anti aliasing effect, and the weaker the pixel jitter

###### render.postProcessing.taa.sharpFactor?

`number`

Image sharpening coefficient [0.1-0.9]: The smaller the coefficient, the weaker the sharpening effect, the better the anti aliasing effect. Conversely, the stronger the sharpening, the weaker the anti aliasing effect

###### render.postProcessing.taa.sharpPreBlurFactor?

`number`

Image sharpening sampling coefficient scaling coefficient: Scales the sampling offset during sharpening.

`boolean`

###### render.postProcessing.depthOfView.pixelOffset?

`number`

the distance of Blur effect pixel diffusion

###### render.postProcessing.depthOfView.near?

`number`

the pixel below this distance to camera will not be blurred

###### render.postProcessing.depthOfView.far?

`number`

the pixel above this distance will experience maximum blurring,

###### render.postProcessing.volumetricFog?

\{ `enable?`: `boolean`; `density?`: `number`; `scatteringIntensity?`: `number`; `anisotropy?`: `number`; `maxDistance?`: `number`; `stepCount?`: `number`; `ambient?`: \{ `r?`: `number`; `g?`: `number`; `b?`: `number`; \}; \}

###### render.postProcessing.volumetricFog.enable?

`boolean`

Whether the post pass runs. Toggled by `addPost` / detach.

###### render.postProcessing.volumetricFog.density?

`number`

Beer-Lambert extinction coefficient per unit distance.
 0.0 disables fog absorption. 0.05 is a good baseline.

###### render.postProcessing.volumetricFog.scatteringIntensity?

`number`

Multiplier on accumulated scattering. Punchier values
 amplify "god rays" near the sun. 1.0 default.

###### render.postProcessing.volumetricFog.anisotropy?

`number`

Henyey-Greenstein phase asymmetry [-0.99, 0.99]. Positive =
 forward scatter (light shafts visible looking toward sun);
 negative = backward; 0 = isotropic. 0.6 is canonical.

###### render.postProcessing.volumetricFog.maxDistance?

`number`

Cap the ray-march distance in world units. Past this,
 transmittance saturates. 100 default.

###### render.postProcessing.volumetricFog.stepCount?

`number`

Number of march steps per pixel. 16 (cheap, banded) → 64
 (smooth, expensive). 32 default.

###### render.postProcessing.volumetricFog.ambient?

\{ `r?`: `number`; `g?`: `number`; `b?`: `number`; \}

Ambient scattering tint added at every step (independent of
 the directional light). Useful for low-key blue night fogs.

###### render.postProcessing.volumetricFog.ambient.r?

`number`

###### render.postProcessing.volumetricFog.ambient.g?

`number`

###### render.postProcessing.volumetricFog.ambient.b?

`number`

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.aspect?

`number`

Canvas aspect ratio (`windowWidth / windowHeight`), recomputed on resize.

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.presentationSize?

`number`[] = `...`

Drawable surface size in physical pixels as `[width, height]`.

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.canvas?

\{ \}

The HTML canvas element this context renders into.

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.context?

\{ \}

The WebGPU canvas context obtained from `canvas.getContext('webgpu')`.

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.windowWidth?

`number`

Canvas backing-store width in physical pixels (clientWidth * pixelRatio).

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.windowHeight?

`number`

Canvas backing-store height in physical pixels (clientHeight * pixelRatio).

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.canvasConfig?

\{ `canvas?`: \{ \}; `alpha?`: `boolean`; `zIndex?`: `number`; `devicePixelRatio?`: `number`; `backgroundImage?`: `string`; \}

The canvas/configuration options supplied to `init()`.

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.canvasConfig.canvas?

\{ \}

reference of canvas

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.canvasConfig.alpha?

`boolean`

wheter use transparent background
To set a transparent background, the SkyRenderer[SkyRenderer](SkyRenderer.md) component should be disabled
skyRender.enable = false

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.canvasConfig.zIndex?

`number`

canvas styler zIndex

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.canvasConfig.devicePixelRatio?

`number`

canvas pixel ratio
use window.devicePixelRatio is not provided

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.canvasConfig.backgroundImage?

`string`

canvas background image
a canvas background when skybox is hide/disabled and CanvasConfig.alpha is true

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.adapter?

\{ \}

The GPUAdapter this context requested during `init()`.

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.device?

\{ \}

The GPUDevice owned by this context; the root handle for all GPU work.

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.presentationFormat?

`GPUTextureFormat`

The format pipelines target — the sRGB view variant, so the
 GPU does the linear→sRGB encode at write time. Must match the
 view created in `GPUContext.beginRenderPass`.

 immediately after constructing this Context3D. Used by per-context
 subsystems (GlobalUniformGroup, RenderShaderPass, ...) to read the
 engine's instance `setting` without needing a view/camera handle.

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.engine.setting?

\{ doublePrecision?: boolean; useRTE?: boolean; RTEScale?: number; occlusionQuery?: \{ enable?: boolean; debug?: boolean; octree?: \{ width?: number; height?: number; depth?: number; x?: number; y?: number; z?: number; \}; \}; ... 8 more ...; reflectionSetting?: \{ ...; \}; \}

Per-engine configuration tree. Defaults live in `Engine3D._defaultSetting()`;
overrides come from `descriptor.setting` at `Engine3D.init()` time and
are deep-merged on top. Mutating at runtime (`engine.setting.shadow.enable = false`)
takes effect on the next frame for values read each frame; values baked
into GPU resources at `create()` time (shadow map dimensions, reflection
probe size, etc.) need re-creation.

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.lost?

`boolean` = `false`

Set to true when the underlying GPUDevice has been lost (driver reset,
 device unplug, tab/iframe suspended, explicit `device.destroy()`...).
 Once lost, the device is permanently unusable — all `_boundCtx`
 resources on this Context3D are stale. The owning Engine3D stops
 scheduling render frames. App code should listen for
 `Context3D.DEVICE_LOST` and call `Engine3D.init()` again to recover.

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.lostInfo?

\{ \} = `null`

The `GPUDeviceLostInfo` captured when the device was lost, else null.

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.gpuContext.lastGeometry.vertexBuffer.bufferChanged?

`boolean` = `false`

Set to `true` whenever `vertexGPUBuffer` is replaced by a fresh
allocation (first build or a packing-size change). Consumers that
captured the GPU buffer handle — e.g. compute pipelines writing
deformed/generated vertices — must observe this flag and rebind,
otherwise they keep writing into an orphaned buffer while the
renderer draws the new one. The owner resets it after handling.

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.gpuContext.lastRenderPassState.camera3D.object3D.transform.scene3D.renderNode.shadowCacheMode?

... = `'auto'`

Shadow cache classification.

- `'auto'` (default): renderer is drawn to the shadow map every frame
  as part of the single-pass render — matches historical behaviour.
- `'static'`: renderer is drawn only to the cached static depth layer,
  rebuilt lazily when the light moves or the scene explicitly marks
  the static cache dirty. Use for buildings, terrain, prop meshes that
  don't move.
- `'dynamic'`: renderer is drawn every frame on top of the copied-in
  static layer. Use for characters, physics objects, anything that
  moves.

Only consulted when `engine.setting.shadow.enableStaticCache === true`;
otherwise all renderers behave as `'auto'`.

overrides come from `descriptor.setting` at `Engine3D.init()` time and
are deep-merged on top. Mutating at runtime (`engine.setting.shadow.enable = false`)
takes effect on the next frame for values read each frame; values baked
into GPU resources at `create()` time (shadow map dimensions, reflection

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.gpuContext.lastRenderPassState.camera3D.object3D.renderNode.geometry.vertexBuffer.bufferChanged?

... = `false`

Set to `true` whenever `vertexGPUBuffer` is replaced by a fresh
allocation (first build or a packing-size change). Consumers that
captured the GPU buffer handle — e.g. compute pipelines writing
deformed/generated vertices — must observe this flag and rebind,
otherwise they keep writing into an orphaned buffer while the
renderer draws the new one. The owner resets it after handling.

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.gpuContext.lastRenderPassState.camera3D.object3D.renderNode.shadowCacheMode?

`"auto"` \| `"static"` \| `"dynamic"` = `'auto'`

Shadow cache classification.

- `'auto'` (default): renderer is drawn to the shadow map every frame
  as part of the single-pass render — matches historical behaviour.
- `'static'`: renderer is drawn only to the cached static depth layer,
  rebuilt lazily when the light moves or the scene explicitly marks
  the static cache dirty. Use for buildings, terrain, prop meshes that
  don't move.
- `'dynamic'`: renderer is drawn every frame on top of the copied-in
  static layer. Use for characters, physics objects, anything that
  moves.

Only consulted when `engine.setting.shadow.enableStaticCache === true`;
otherwise all renderers behave as `'auto'`.

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.gpuContext.lastRenderPassState.camera3D.object3D.parent.scene3D.renderNode.shadowCacheMode?

... = `'auto'`

Shadow cache classification.

- `'auto'` (default): renderer is drawn to the shadow map every frame
  as part of the single-pass render — matches historical behaviour.
- `'static'`: renderer is drawn only to the cached static depth layer,
  rebuilt lazily when the light moves or the scene explicitly marks
  the static cache dirty. Use for buildings, terrain, prop meshes that
  don't move.
- `'dynamic'`: renderer is drawn every frame on top of the copied-in
  static layer. Use for characters, physics objects, anything that
  moves.

Only consulted when `engine.setting.shadow.enableStaticCache === true`;
otherwise all renderers behave as `'auto'`.

into GPU resources at `create()` time (shadow map dimensions, reflection

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.gpuContext.lastRenderPassState.camera3D.transform.object3D.renderNode.shadowCacheMode?

... \| ... \| ... = `'auto'`

Shadow cache classification.

- `'auto'` (default): renderer is drawn to the shadow map every frame
  as part of the single-pass render — matches historical behaviour.
- `'static'`: renderer is drawn only to the cached static depth layer,
  rebuilt lazily when the light moves or the scene explicitly marks
  the static cache dirty. Use for buildings, terrain, prop meshes that
  don't move.
- `'dynamic'`: renderer is drawn every frame on top of the copied-in
  static layer. Use for characters, physics objects, anything that
  moves.

Only consulted when `engine.setting.shadow.enableStaticCache === true`;
otherwise all renderers behave as `'auto'`.

overrides come from `descriptor.setting` at `Engine3D.init()` time and
are deep-merged on top. Mutating at runtime (`engine.setting.shadow.enable = false`)
takes effect on the next frame for values read each frame; values baked
into GPU resources at `create()` time (shadow map dimensions, reflection
probe size, etc.) need re-creation.

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.gpuContext.lastRenderPassState.camera3D.transform.scene3D.renderNode.shadowCacheMode?

... \| ... \| ... = `'auto'`

Shadow cache classification.

- `'auto'` (default): renderer is drawn to the shadow map every frame
  as part of the single-pass render — matches historical behaviour.
- `'static'`: renderer is drawn only to the cached static depth layer,
  rebuilt lazily when the light moves or the scene explicitly marks
  the static cache dirty. Use for buildings, terrain, prop meshes that
  don't move.
- `'dynamic'`: renderer is drawn every frame on top of the copied-in
  static layer. Use for characters, physics objects, anything that
  moves.

Only consulted when `engine.setting.shadow.enableStaticCache === true`;
otherwise all renderers behave as `'auto'`.

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.gpuContext.lastRenderPassState.camera3D.transform.scene3D.parentObject.renderNode.shadowCacheMode?

... = `'auto'`

Shadow cache classification.

- `'auto'` (default): renderer is drawn to the shadow map every frame
  as part of the single-pass render — matches historical behaviour.
- `'static'`: renderer is drawn only to the cached static depth layer,
  rebuilt lazily when the light moves or the scene explicitly marks
  the static cache dirty. Use for buildings, terrain, prop meshes that
  don't move.
- `'dynamic'`: renderer is drawn every frame on top of the copied-in
  static layer. Use for characters, physics objects, anything that
  moves.

Only consulted when `engine.setting.shadow.enableStaticCache === true`;
otherwise all renderers behave as `'auto'`.

Per-engine configuration tree. Defaults live in `Engine3D._defaultSetting()`;
overrides come from `descriptor.setting` at `Engine3D.init()` time and
are deep-merged on top. Mutating at runtime (`engine.setting.shadow.enable = false`)
takes effect on the next frame for values read each frame; values baked
into GPU resources at `create()` time (shadow map dimensions, reflection
probe size, etc.) need re-creation.

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.gpuContext.lastRenderPassState.camera3D.transform.view3D.scene.renderNode.shadowCacheMode?

... = `'auto'`

Shadow cache classification.

- `'auto'` (default): renderer is drawn to the shadow map every frame
  as part of the single-pass render — matches historical behaviour.
- `'static'`: renderer is drawn only to the cached static depth layer,
  rebuilt lazily when the light moves or the scene explicitly marks
  the static cache dirty. Use for buildings, terrain, prop meshes that
  don't move.
- `'dynamic'`: renderer is drawn every frame on top of the copied-in
  static layer. Use for characters, physics objects, anything that
  moves.

Only consulted when `engine.setting.shadow.enableStaticCache === true`;
otherwise all renderers behave as `'auto'`.

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.gpuContext.lastRenderPassState.camera3D.shadowLight.transform.object3D.renderNode.shadowCacheMode?

... = `'auto'`

Shadow cache classification.

- `'auto'` (default): renderer is drawn to the shadow map every frame
  as part of the single-pass render — matches historical behaviour.
- `'static'`: renderer is drawn only to the cached static depth layer,
  rebuilt lazily when the light moves or the scene explicitly marks
  the static cache dirty. Use for buildings, terrain, prop meshes that
  don't move.
- `'dynamic'`: renderer is drawn every frame on top of the copied-in
  static layer. Use for characters, physics objects, anything that
  moves.

Only consulted when `engine.setting.shadow.enableStaticCache === true`;
otherwise all renderers behave as `'auto'`.

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.gpuContext.lastRenderPassState.camera3D.shadowLight.transform.scene3D.renderNode.shadowCacheMode?

... = `'auto'`

Shadow cache classification.

- `'auto'` (default): renderer is drawn to the shadow map every frame
  as part of the single-pass render — matches historical behaviour.
- `'static'`: renderer is drawn only to the cached static depth layer,
  rebuilt lazily when the light moves or the scene explicitly marks
  the static cache dirty. Use for buildings, terrain, prop meshes that
  don't move.
- `'dynamic'`: renderer is drawn every frame on top of the copied-in
  static layer. Use for characters, physics objects, anything that
  moves.

Only consulted when `engine.setting.shadow.enableStaticCache === true`;
otherwise all renderers behave as `'auto'`.

into GPU resources at `create()` time (shadow map dimensions, reflection

###### sky.sky._boundCtx.gpuContext.lastRenderPassState.camera3D.cullingMask?

`number` = `VisibleLayer.All`

Layer-mask of layers this camera should see. Combined at pass
execute time with `node.visibleLayer` and the active pass's
`layerMask` via bitwise AND:

    (node.visibleLayer & pass.layerMask & camera.cullingMask) !== 0

Defaults to [VisibleLayer.All](../@orillusion/namespaces/VisibleLayer/variables/All.md) so untouched cameras keep
the historical "see everything" behaviour. Sub-cameras
(minimaps, reflection probes, picking-only views) can clear
specific bits to suppress unwanted layers.

Camera-side filtering is layered on top of pass-side filtering:
a layer must clear both masks AND the node's own membership to
be drawn.

\{ `debug?`: `any`; `enable?`: `boolean`; `needUpdate?`: `boolean`; `autoUpdate?`: `boolean`; `updateFrameRate?`: `number`; `type?`: `"PCF"` \| `"HARD"` \| `"SOFT"`; `shadowSize?`: `number`; `shadowSoft?`: `number`; `pcfKernelScale?`: `number`; `pointShadowSize?`: `number`; `csmMargin?`: `number`; `csmScatteringExp?`: `number`; `csmAreaScale?`: `number`; `maxShadowMapNum?`: `number`; `maxShadowMapWidth?`: `number`; `maxShadowMapHeight?`: `number`; `maxCascades?`: `number`; `shadowBound?`: `number`; `enableStaticCache?`: `boolean`; `contactShadow?`: \{ `enable?`: `boolean`; `maxStepCount?`: `number`; `maxDistance?`: `number`; `thickness?`: `number`; `bias?`: `number`; `intensity?`: `number`; \}; \}

###### shadow.debug?

enable

###### shadow.autoUpdate?

update shadown automatic

###### shadow.updateFrameRate?

frequency for shadows update

###### shadow.type?

`"PCF"` \| `"HARD"` \| `"SOFT"`

Shadow sampling mode.

- `'HARD'`: single-tap hardware compare, sharp 1-texel edges.
  Cheapest. Default.
- `'PCF'`: 3×3 tent-weighted PCF (~5×5 effective via the
  hardware comparison sampler's 2×2 filtering). Mild softness,
  uniform across the shadow map regardless of receiver depth.
- `'SOFT'`: **Percentage-Closer Soft Shadows (PCSS)** — the
  16-tap blocker search + similar-triangles penumbra estimate +
  16-tap Poisson PCF. Produces "contact hardening": sharp
  directly under occluders, progressively softer as receiver-to-
  blocker distance grows. The most expensive of the three but
  the only one that captures distance-dependent softness.
  Per-light `softness` (light.size in shadow-map texels) overrides
  the global `shadowSoft` knob.

###### shadow.shadowSize?

`number`

shadow mapping Size

###### shadow.shadowSoft?

`number`

Shadow softness

###### shadow.pcfKernelScale?

`number`

Directional PCF kernel radius multiplier. 1.0 = exactly one shadow
texel per sample step (3x3 tap spacing). Values > 1 widen the
kernel for softer edges at the cost of possible peter-panning;
values < 1 tighten it and give sharper but more aliased edges.
Live-tunable — the value is rewritten to globalUniform every frame.
Default 1.0.

###### shadow.pointShadowSize?

`number`

Point shadow mapping size

###### shadow.csmMargin?

`number`

Blend Shadow(0-1)

###### shadow.csmScatteringExp?

`number`

scattering csm Area Exponent for each level

###### shadow.csmAreaScale?

`number`

scale csm Area of all level

###### shadow.maxShadowMapNum?

`number`

max shadow map number

###### shadow.maxShadowMapWidth?

`number`

max shadow map width

###### shadow.maxShadowMapHeight?

`number`

max shadow map height

###### shadow.maxCascades?

`number`

max cascades for csm

###### shadow.shadowBound?

`number`

shadow bound, the area of shadow map projection,
the larger the value, the more area the shadow map covers,
but the lower the quality.
The smaller the value, the higher the quality,
but the smaller the area covered by the shadow map.
It is recommended to set this value according to the
scene size and light distance.

###### shadow.enableStaticCache?

`boolean`

Opt-in static-shadow caching.

When `true`, the shadow-cast pass splits into two phases per frame:
  1. If the per-light static layer is dirty (light moved, or the scene
     explicitly marked dirty), rebuild it by drawing only renderers
     with `shadowCacheMode === 'static'`. Result stored in a cached
     depth texture.
  2. Every frame: copy the cached static depth into the live shadow
     map and draw renderers with `shadowCacheMode === 'dynamic'` on
     top (load-op preserves the copied depth, allowing correct
     occlusion resolution between static and dynamic geometry).

When `false` (default), all renderers are treated as dynamic and the
pipeline behaves exactly like before — no cached layer, no extra
copies. Safe default for backwards compatibility.

Only `'auto'` / `'static'` / `'dynamic'` tags on `RenderNode.shadowCacheMode`
are consulted when this flag is on; `'auto'` counts as dynamic.

###### shadow.contactShadow?

\{ `enable?`: `boolean`; `maxStepCount?`: `number`; `maxDistance?`: `number`; `thickness?`: `number`; `bias?`: `number`; `intensity?`: `number`; \}

Contact Shadows — short screen-space ray-march along the dominant
 directional light. Adds the close-contact darkness CSM can't
 resolve (object-on-floor, fingers-on-table). Enable by adding
 ContactShadowPost to the post chain; this sub-tree controls
 the shader parameters.

###### shadow.contactShadow.enable?

`boolean`

###### shadow.contactShadow.maxStepCount?

`number`

Number of ray-march steps. 12-24 is the visual sweet-spot.

###### shadow.contactShadow.maxDistance?

`number`

World-space ray length. Smaller = tighter contact-only shadow.

###### shadow.contactShadow.thickness?

`number`

Depth-difference window that counts as "occluded". Bigger
 catches more contact but smears under thin geometry.

###### shadow.contactShadow.bias?

`number`

Bias along the surface normal to avoid self-shadow acne.

###### shadow.contactShadow.intensity?

`number`

[0,1] strength.

### setting

> `readonly` **setting**: [`EngineSetting`](../type-aliases/EngineSetting.md)

Defined in: [src/Engine3D.ts:293](https://github.com/orillusion/orillusion/blob/main/src/Engine3D.ts#L293)

Per-engine configuration tree. Defaults live in `Engine3D._defaultSetting()`;
overrides come from `descriptor.setting` at `Engine3D.init()` time and
are deep-merged on top. Mutating at runtime (`engine.setting.shadow.enable = false`)
takes effect on the next frame for values read each frame; values baked
into GPU resources at `create()` time (shadow map dimensions, reflection
probe size, etc.) need re-creation.

## Methods

### resFor()

> `static` **resFor**(`ctx?`): [`Res`](Res.md)

Defined in: [src/Engine3D.ts:238](https://github.com/orillusion/orillusion/blob/main/src/Engine3D.ts#L238)

Per-Context3D Res accessor. Pass the owning engine's `context3D`
explicitly to target a specific device.

When `ctx` is omitted AND exactly one Engine3D has been created,
falls back to that engine's context — keeps the single-engine path
(`new LitMaterial()`, etc.) ergonomic. For multi-engine apps the
caller MUST pass `ctx`; otherwise this throws because picking one
arbitrarily would silently bind resources to the wrong device.

The `Res` instance is cached before `initDefault()` runs because
`initDefault()` creates a `LitMaterial` whose default shader reads
`engine.res` recursively — the re-entrant call must see the same
(partially-initialized) instance instead of looping the factory.

#### Parameters

##### ctx?

[`Context3D`](Context3D.md)

#### Returns

[`Res`](Res.md)

###### setting.render.gpuCull?

`boolean`

GPU-driven culling — when true, frustum + (when paired with
 Hi-Z) occlusion tests run on the GPU per mesh instance and
 produce a `drawIndexedIndirect` arg buffer. The compute pass
 is fully implemented in `GPUCullPass` / `GPUFrustumCull_cs`;
 what's still skeleton is the `drawNodes` consumer
 (`_transparentDraw.ts`, driven by `ColorPass`) that actually
 issues the indirect call (the existing per-node iteration
 coexists). Flip this on AND open the integration in `drawNodes`
 to get the 5-20× perf win.

###### setting.render.msaa?

`0` \| `2` \| `4` \| `8`

Per-instance MSAA sample count for the main color pass.
 0 disables MSAA (default). Valid non-zero values: 2 | 4 | 8
 depending on device support. Enabling MSAA unlocks
 alpha-to-coverage (set LitMaterial.alphaMode = 'MASK').

###### setting.render.useOIT?

`boolean`

Opt-in order-independent transparency (Weighted Blended OIT).
 When true, materials with `oitMode === 'weighted'` are routed
 through the OIT accum/resolve features instead of the sorted
 transparent path. Default false — matches legacy behavior.

###### setting.render.decals?

`boolean`

Opt-in projected decals. When true, ForwardRendererJob inserts
 `DecalShadowVolumePass` between the opaque/transmission half and
 the sorted transparent half — every active `DecalComponent`
 projects its texture onto the opaque scene via stencil shadow
 volumes. Default false.

###### setting.render.useStencil?

`boolean`

Opt-in 8-bit stencil buffer on the main color pass.
 When true, `GBufferFrame` allocates its depth attachment as
 `depth24plus-stencil8` instead of the default `depth32float`,
 so material-level stencil state (`Material.stencilFront/Back/
 ReadMask/WriteMask/Ref`) is actually validated and bound at
 pipeline build time. Off by default — adding stencil makes the
 depth attachment incompatible with depth-only sampling paths
 (SSR/SSGI/Outline read `_MainDepthTexture` as `sampleType: depth`),
 so opt in only when the project actually needs stencil and the
 z-prepass is disabled (`zPrePass: false`) — the prepass path
 routes the color pass through a separate `depth32float`
 `zPreTexture` and the stencil attachment is silently dropped.

###### setting.render.tonemap?

\{ `enable?`: `boolean`; `exposure?`: `number`; `mode?`: `"ACES"` \| `"None"`; \}

Final HDR→LDR tonemap. Runs after every other post (Bloom,
FXAA, GodRay, etc.) so the ACES curve sees the composited HDR
signal. Setting `enable=false` reverts to a passthrough pass —
lighting and bloom shaders no longer apply inline ACES, so the
frame will be raw HDR clamped at swapchain encode time.

###### setting.render.tonemap.enable?

`boolean`

Master switch. When false, the post is still attached but
 acts as a straight passthrough — useful for A/B comparisons.

###### setting.render.tonemap.exposure?

`number`

Linear scale multiplied onto the HDR color before the curve.
 1.0 is the neutral default (no exposure compensation).

###### setting.render.tonemap.mode?

`"ACES"` \| `"None"`

Curve selector. 'ACES' applies the Filmic Narkowicz fit;
 'None' is straight passthrough (same effect as enable=false
 but keeps exposure scaling).

enable

###### setting.render.postProcessing.ssr.mixThreshold?

###### setting.render.postProcessing.taa?

\{ `enable?`: `boolean`; `jitterSeedCount?`: `number`; `blendFactor?`: `number`; `temporalJitterScale?`: `number`; `sharpFactor?`: `number`; `sharpPreBlurFactor?`: `number`; `debug?`: `boolean`; \}

###### setting.render.postProcessing.taa.enable?

`boolean`

###### setting.render.postProcessing.taa.jitterSeedCount?

`number`

The number of random seed for dithering camera is 8 by default.
Reducing the number can solve some problems with noticeable jitter, but the jagginess will become more pronounced

###### setting.render.postProcessing.taa.blendFactor?

`number`

Merge the coefficients of the historical frame and the current frame. The smaller the parameter, the smaller the proportion of the current frame

###### setting.render.postProcessing.taa.temporalJitterScale?

`number`

The scaling coefficient of the random offset value of the jitter camera [0,1]: The smaller the coefficient, the weaker the anti aliasing effect, and the weaker the pixel jitter

###### setting.render.postProcessing.taa.sharpFactor?

`number`

Image sharpening coefficient [0.1-0.9]: The smaller the coefficient, the weaker the sharpening effect, the better the anti aliasing effect. Conversely, the stronger the sharpening, the weaker the anti aliasing effect

###### setting.render.postProcessing.taa.sharpPreBlurFactor?

`number`

Image sharpening sampling coefficient scaling coefficient: Scales the sampling offset during sharpening.

###### setting.render.postProcessing.taa.debug?

`boolean`

###### setting.render.postProcessing.gtao?

###### setting.render.postProcessing.gtao.enable?

`boolean`

###### setting.render.postProcessing.gtao.maxDistance?

`number`

Set the maximum distance to search around 3D space during ao sampling

###### setting.render.postProcessing.gtao.maxPixel?

`number`

Set the maximum distance when searching for surrounding pixels during ao sampling

###### setting.render.postProcessing.gtao.darkFactor?

`number`

Set the coefficient of ao value to participate in outputting to the screen, 1: output all, 0: not output

###### setting.render.postProcessing.gtao.rayMarchSegment?

`number`

Set the number of steps for AO sampling. A larger value will result in better quality AO effects while consuming more performance

###### setting.render.postProcessing.gtao.multiBounce?

`boolean`

Simulate color rebound or not

###### setting.render.postProcessing.gtao.usePosFloat32?

`boolean`

true: Calculate the position value of GBuffer using f32 to obtain more accurate values (water and other effects may not be supported)
false: We will use the position value of GBuffer in f16 for operations, with a wider coverage

###### setting.render.postProcessing.gtao.blendColor?

`boolean`

True: will be mixed with the mainColor of GBuffer; False: will only output the colors of ao

###### setting.render.postProcessing.gtao.debug?

`boolean`

###### setting.render.postProcessing.depthOfView.near?

###### setting.render.postProcessing.volumetricFog?

\{ `enable?`: `boolean`; `density?`: `number`; `scatteringIntensity?`: `number`; `anisotropy?`: `number`; `maxDistance?`: `number`; `stepCount?`: `number`; `ambient?`: \{ `r?`: `number`; `g?`: `number`; `b?`: `number`; \}; \}

###### setting.render.postProcessing.volumetricFog.enable?

`boolean`

Whether the post pass runs. Toggled by `addPost` / detach.

###### setting.render.postProcessing.volumetricFog.density?

`number`

Beer-Lambert extinction coefficient per unit distance.
 0.0 disables fog absorption. 0.05 is a good baseline.

###### setting.render.postProcessing.volumetricFog.scatteringIntensity?

`number`

Multiplier on accumulated scattering. Punchier values
 amplify "god rays" near the sun. 1.0 default.

###### setting.render.postProcessing.volumetricFog.anisotropy?

`number`

Henyey-Greenstein phase asymmetry [-0.99, 0.99]. Positive =
 forward scatter (light shafts visible looking toward sun);
 negative = backward; 0 = isotropic. 0.6 is canonical.

###### setting.render.postProcessing.volumetricFog.maxDistance?

`number`

Cap the ray-march distance in world units. Past this,
 transmittance saturates. 100 default.

###### setting.render.postProcessing.volumetricFog.stepCount?

`number`

Number of march steps per pixel. 16 (cheap, banded) → 64
 (smooth, expensive). 32 default.

###### setting.render.postProcessing.volumetricFog.ambient?

\{ `r?`: `number`; `g?`: `number`; `b?`: `number`; \}

Ambient scattering tint added at every step (independent of
 the directional light). Useful for low-key blue night fogs.

###### setting.render.postProcessing.volumetricFog.ambient.r?

`number`

###### setting.render.postProcessing.volumetricFog.ambient.g?

`number`

###### setting.render.postProcessing.volumetricFog.ambient.b?

`number`

###### setting.sky.sky._boundCtx.aspect?

`number`

Canvas aspect ratio (`windowWidth / windowHeight`), recomputed on resize.

###### setting.sky.sky._boundCtx.presentationSize?

`number`[] = `...`

Drawable surface size in physical pixels as `[width, height]`.

###### setting.sky.sky._boundCtx.canvas?

\{ \}

The HTML canvas element this context renders into.

###### setting.sky.sky._boundCtx.context?

\{ \}

The WebGPU canvas context obtained from `canvas.getContext('webgpu')`.

###### setting.sky.sky._boundCtx.windowWidth?

`number`

Canvas backing-store width in physical pixels (clientWidth * pixelRatio).

###### setting.sky.sky._boundCtx.windowHeight?

`number`

Canvas backing-store height in physical pixels (clientHeight * pixelRatio).

###### setting.sky.sky._boundCtx.canvasConfig?

\{ `canvas?`: \{ \}; `alpha?`: `boolean`; `zIndex?`: `number`; `devicePixelRatio?`: `number`; `backgroundImage?`: `string`; \}

The canvas/configuration options supplied to `init()`.

###### setting.sky.sky._boundCtx.canvasConfig.canvas?

\{ \}

reference of canvas

###### setting.sky.sky._boundCtx.canvasConfig.alpha?

`boolean`

wheter use transparent background
To set a transparent background, the SkyRenderer[SkyRenderer](SkyRenderer.md) component should be disabled
skyRender.enable = false

###### setting.sky.sky._boundCtx.canvasConfig.zIndex?

`number`

canvas styler zIndex

###### setting.sky.sky._boundCtx.canvasConfig.devicePixelRatio?

`number`

canvas pixel ratio
use window.devicePixelRatio is not provided

###### setting.sky.sky._boundCtx.canvasConfig.backgroundImage?

`string`

canvas background image
a canvas background when skybox is hide/disabled and CanvasConfig.alpha is true

###### setting.sky.sky._boundCtx.adapter?

\{ \}

The GPUAdapter this context requested during `init()`.

###### setting.sky.sky._boundCtx.device?

\{ \}

The GPUDevice owned by this context; the root handle for all GPU work.

###### setting.sky.sky._boundCtx.presentationFormat?

`GPUTextureFormat`

The format pipelines target — the sRGB view variant, so the
 GPU does the linear→sRGB encode at write time. Must match the
 view created in `GPUContext.beginRenderPass`.

Back-reference to the owning Engine3D. Populated by `new Engine3D()`
 immediately after constructing this Context3D. Used by per-context
 subsystems (GlobalUniformGroup, RenderShaderPass, ...) to read the
 engine's instance `setting` without needing a view/camera handle.

###### setting.sky.sky._boundCtx.engine.setting?

\{ doublePrecision?: boolean; useRTE?: boolean; RTEScale?: number; occlusionQuery?: \{ enable?: boolean; debug?: boolean; octree?: \{ width?: number; height?: number; depth?: number; x?: number; y?: number; z?: number; \}; \}; ... 8 more ...; reflectionSetting?: \{ ...; \}; \}

Per-engine configuration tree. Defaults live in `Engine3D._defaultSetting()`;
overrides come from `descriptor.setting` at `Engine3D.init()` time and
are deep-merged on top. Mutating at runtime (`engine.setting.shadow.enable = false`)
takes effect on the next frame for values read each frame; values baked
into GPU resources at `create()` time (shadow map dimensions, reflection
probe size, etc.) need re-creation.

###### setting.sky.sky._boundCtx.lost?

`boolean` = `false`

Set to true when the underlying GPUDevice has been lost (driver reset,
 device unplug, tab/iframe suspended, explicit `device.destroy()`...).
 Once lost, the device is permanently unusable — all `_boundCtx`
 resources on this Context3D are stale. The owning Engine3D stops
 scheduling render frames. App code should listen for
 `Context3D.DEVICE_LOST` and call `Engine3D.init()` again to recover.

###### setting.sky.sky._boundCtx.lostInfo?

\{ \} = `null`

The `GPUDeviceLostInfo` captured when the device was lost, else null.

###### setting.sky.sky._boundCtx.gpuContext.lastGeometry.vertexBuffer.bufferChanged?

`boolean` = `false`

Set to `true` whenever `vertexGPUBuffer` is replaced by a fresh
allocation (first build or a packing-size change). Consumers that
captured the GPU buffer handle — e.g. compute pipelines writing
deformed/generated vertices — must observe this flag and rebind,
otherwise they keep writing into an orphaned buffer while the
renderer draws the new one. The owner resets it after handling.

###### setting.sky.sky._boundCtx.gpuContext.lastRenderPassState.camera3D.object3D.renderNode.shadowCacheMode?

... \| ... \| ... = `'auto'`

Shadow cache classification.

- `'auto'` (default): renderer is drawn to the shadow map every frame
  as part of the single-pass render — matches historical behaviour.
- `'static'`: renderer is drawn only to the cached static depth layer,
  rebuilt lazily when the light moves or the scene explicitly marks
  the static cache dirty. Use for buildings, terrain, prop meshes that
  don't move.
- `'dynamic'`: renderer is drawn every frame on top of the copied-in
  static layer. Use for characters, physics objects, anything that
  moves.

Only consulted when `engine.setting.shadow.enableStaticCache === true`;
otherwise all renderers behave as `'auto'`.

###### setting.sky.sky._boundCtx.gpuContext.lastRenderPassState.camera3D.transform.object3D.renderNode.shadowCacheMode?

... = `'auto'`

Shadow cache classification.

- `'auto'` (default): renderer is drawn to the shadow map every frame
  as part of the single-pass render — matches historical behaviour.
- `'static'`: renderer is drawn only to the cached static depth layer,
  rebuilt lazily when the light moves or the scene explicitly marks
  the static cache dirty. Use for buildings, terrain, prop meshes that
  don't move.
- `'dynamic'`: renderer is drawn every frame on top of the copied-in
  static layer. Use for characters, physics objects, anything that
  moves.

Only consulted when `engine.setting.shadow.enableStaticCache === true`;
otherwise all renderers behave as `'auto'`.

###### setting.sky.sky._boundCtx.gpuContext.lastRenderPassState.camera3D.transform.scene3D.renderNode.shadowCacheMode?

... = `'auto'`

Shadow cache classification.

- `'auto'` (default): renderer is drawn to the shadow map every frame
  as part of the single-pass render — matches historical behaviour.
- `'static'`: renderer is drawn only to the cached static depth layer,
  rebuilt lazily when the light moves or the scene explicitly marks
  the static cache dirty. Use for buildings, terrain, prop meshes that
  don't move.
- `'dynamic'`: renderer is drawn every frame on top of the copied-in
  static layer. Use for characters, physics objects, anything that
  moves.

Only consulted when `engine.setting.shadow.enableStaticCache === true`;
otherwise all renderers behave as `'auto'`.

overrides come from `descriptor.setting` at `Engine3D.init()` time and

takes effect on the next frame for values read each frame; values baked
into GPU resources at `create()` time (shadow map dimensions, reflection

###### setting.sky.sky._boundCtx.gpuContext.lastRenderPassState.camera3D.cullingMask?

`number` = `VisibleLayer.All`

Layer-mask of layers this camera should see. Combined at pass
execute time with `node.visibleLayer` and the active pass's
`layerMask` via bitwise AND:

    (node.visibleLayer & pass.layerMask & camera.cullingMask) !== 0

Defaults to [VisibleLayer.All](../@orillusion/namespaces/VisibleLayer/variables/All.md) so untouched cameras keep
the historical "see everything" behaviour. Sub-cameras
(minimaps, reflection probes, picking-only views) can clear
specific bits to suppress unwanted layers.

Camera-side filtering is layered on top of pass-side filtering:
a layer must clear both masks AND the node's own membership to
be drawn.

###### setting.shadow?

\{ `debug?`: `any`; `enable?`: `boolean`; `needUpdate?`: `boolean`; `autoUpdate?`: `boolean`; `updateFrameRate?`: `number`; `type?`: `"PCF"` \| `"HARD"` \| `"SOFT"`; `shadowSize?`: `number`; `shadowSoft?`: `number`; `pcfKernelScale?`: `number`; `pointShadowSize?`: `number`; `csmMargin?`: `number`; `csmScatteringExp?`: `number`; `csmAreaScale?`: `number`; `maxShadowMapNum?`: `number`; `maxShadowMapWidth?`: `number`; `maxShadowMapHeight?`: `number`; `maxCascades?`: `number`; `shadowBound?`: `number`; `enableStaticCache?`: `boolean`; `contactShadow?`: \{ `enable?`: `boolean`; `maxStepCount?`: `number`; `maxDistance?`: `number`; `thickness?`: `number`; `bias?`: `number`; `intensity?`: `number`; \}; \}

shadow setting

###### setting.shadow.debug?

`any`

###### setting.shadow.enable?

`boolean`

enable

###### setting.shadow.needUpdate?

`boolean`

###### setting.shadow.autoUpdate?

`boolean`

update shadown automatic

###### setting.shadow.updateFrameRate?

`number`

frequency for shadows update

###### setting.shadow.type?

`"PCF"` \| `"HARD"` \| `"SOFT"`

Shadow sampling mode.

- `'HARD'`: single-tap hardware compare, sharp 1-texel edges.
  Cheapest. Default.
- `'PCF'`: 3×3 tent-weighted PCF (~5×5 effective via the
  hardware comparison sampler's 2×2 filtering). Mild softness,
  uniform across the shadow map regardless of receiver depth.
- `'SOFT'`: **Percentage-Closer Soft Shadows (PCSS)** — the
  16-tap blocker search + similar-triangles penumbra estimate +
  16-tap Poisson PCF. Produces "contact hardening": sharp
  directly under occluders, progressively softer as receiver-to-
  blocker distance grows. The most expensive of the three but
  the only one that captures distance-dependent softness.
  Per-light `softness` (light.size in shadow-map texels) overrides
  the global `shadowSoft` knob.

###### setting.shadow.shadowSize?

`number`

shadow mapping Size

###### setting.shadow.shadowSoft?

`number`

Shadow softness

###### setting.shadow.pcfKernelScale?

`number`

Directional PCF kernel radius multiplier. 1.0 = exactly one shadow
texel per sample step (3x3 tap spacing). Values > 1 widen the
kernel for softer edges at the cost of possible peter-panning;
values < 1 tighten it and give sharper but more aliased edges.
Live-tunable — the value is rewritten to globalUniform every frame.
Default 1.0.

###### setting.shadow.pointShadowSize?

`number`

Point shadow mapping size

###### setting.shadow.csmMargin?

`number`

Blend Shadow(0-1)

###### setting.shadow.csmScatteringExp?

`number`

scattering csm Area Exponent for each level

###### setting.shadow.csmAreaScale?

`number`

scale csm Area of all level

###### setting.shadow.maxShadowMapNum?

`number`

max shadow map number

###### setting.shadow.maxShadowMapWidth?

`number`

max shadow map width

###### setting.shadow.maxShadowMapHeight?

`number`

max shadow map height

###### setting.shadow.maxCascades?

`number`

max cascades for csm

###### setting.shadow.shadowBound?

`number`

shadow bound, the area of shadow map projection,
the larger the value, the more area the shadow map covers,
but the lower the quality.
The smaller the value, the higher the quality,
but the smaller the area covered by the shadow map.
It is recommended to set this value according to the
scene size and light distance.

###### setting.shadow.enableStaticCache?

`boolean`

Opt-in static-shadow caching.

When `true`, the shadow-cast pass splits into two phases per frame:
  1. If the per-light static layer is dirty (light moved, or the scene
     explicitly marked dirty), rebuild it by drawing only renderers
     with `shadowCacheMode === 'static'`. Result stored in a cached
     depth texture.
  2. Every frame: copy the cached static depth into the live shadow
     map and draw renderers with `shadowCacheMode === 'dynamic'` on
     top (load-op preserves the copied depth, allowing correct
     occlusion resolution between static and dynamic geometry).

When `false` (default), all renderers are treated as dynamic and the
pipeline behaves exactly like before — no cached layer, no extra
copies. Safe default for backwards compatibility.

Only `'auto'` / `'static'` / `'dynamic'` tags on `RenderNode.shadowCacheMode`
are consulted when this flag is on; `'auto'` counts as dynamic.

###### setting.shadow.contactShadow?

\{ `enable?`: `boolean`; `maxStepCount?`: `number`; `maxDistance?`: `number`; `thickness?`: `number`; `bias?`: `number`; `intensity?`: `number`; \}

Contact Shadows — short screen-space ray-march along the dominant
 directional light. Adds the close-contact darkness CSM can't
 resolve (object-on-floor, fingers-on-table). Enable by adding
 ContactShadowPost to the post chain; this sub-tree controls
 the shader parameters.

###### setting.shadow.contactShadow.enable?

`boolean`

###### setting.shadow.contactShadow.maxStepCount?

`number`

Number of ray-march steps. 12-24 is the visual sweet-spot.

###### setting.shadow.contactShadow.maxDistance?

`number`

World-space ray length. Smaller = tighter contact-only shadow.

###### setting.shadow.contactShadow.thickness?

`number`

Depth-difference window that counts as "occluded". Bigger
 catches more contact but smears under thin geometry.

###### setting.shadow.contactShadow.bias?

`number`

Bias along the surface normal to avoid self-shadow acne.

###### setting.shadow.contactShadow.intensity?

`number`

[0,1] strength.

### dispose()

> **dispose**(): `void`

Defined in: [src/Engine3D.ts:411](https://github.com/orillusion/orillusion/blob/main/src/Engine3D.ts#L411)

Release this engine's GPU device, DOM canvas, ResizeObserver and
input listeners. Required for long-running apps that create/drop
engines (tests, editor previews, modal viewers) — without it, the
browser's per-origin GPU adapter pool is exhausted after a handful
of iterations. Safe to call more than once.

#### Returns

`void`
